objective: Build the missing robot-drive energy and braking foundation from mechanical energy through DC-link headroom, runtime sink allocation, brake chopper, common bus, contactor lifecycle and commissioning, then reconstruct ABB Technical Guide No. 8 with source values separated from robot adaptation.

request_interpretation.curriculum_intent: Continue the bottom-up robotics chain after FOC, power electronics and the TIDA-010956 board, closing the question of where regenerated energy goes during a requested stop.
request_interpretation.depth_intent: Write a private compound failure first and require the public article to supply enough causal insight to solve every premise without printing the problem as a quiz.
request_interpretation.reference_intent: Treat company technical guides as source spines when they provide durable mechanism and selection logic; preserve document revision, example conditions and unsupported transfer boundaries.
request_interpretation.formula_intent: Every display equation has Korean operation reasons inside KaTeX and exactly one FormulaNote. Long operations are split before text is shrunk.
request_interpretation.visual_intent: Use a different representation for topology, four-quadrant state, time headroom, feasibility intervals, common-bus allocation, contactor states and evidence gates. A color-only change is rejected.
request_interpretation.small_model_intent: Retain enough claim, source, boundary, repair and QA state to replay one claim-formula-Viz packet with a 4B model or one causal section with a 9B model.

existing_coverage: robot-motor-drive-foc explains four-quadrant torque and current control
robot-power-electronics-motor-driver explains the DC link, switch path, sensing, protection and board bring-up
reference-ti-tida-010956-2025 provides a concrete 48 V robot inverter boundary
missing_chain: mechanical rotational, translational, gravitational and elastic energy inventory
peak power versus pulse energy versus repeated average power
runtime battery, source, peer-axis and dump-sink availability
multi-axis common-bus arbitration under simultaneous braking
precharge, main contactor, isolation and discharge state evidence
commissioning that closes mechanical and electrical energy ledgers

scope_split.decision: Separate energy and braking from isolation, EMC and certified functional safety.
scope_split.reason: Energy routing needs mechanics, bus and thermal duty reasoning. Isolation/EMC/STO needs insulation coordination, interference paths, redundant shutdown architecture, diagnostic coverage and standards evidence. Combining both would make one article too broad to support a hard transfer problem or readable Viz sequence.
scope_split.deferred_milestone: Robot Drive Isolation, EMC & Functional Safety with TIDA-01599 as a company-reference spine.

private_transfer_gate.scenario: A 48 V multi-axis robot must stop while descending with reflected inertia and a spring load. The battery charge allowance can vanish, the bench supply cannot sink current, every axis can regenerate together, the brake resistor is selected from average watts, contactors are sequenced by timers, only source-side voltage is measured, discharge is assumed after a command, and a battery disconnect occurs during regeneration.
required_insight_groups: declare one mechanics and electrical sign boundary
inventory all stored energy without double counting
separate peak power, event energy and repeated average
derive capacitor headroom from squared voltage and turn it into a deadline
build resistor lower and upper bounds plus pulse and thermal gates
treat peer-axis demand as measured reuse rather than guaranteed future absorption
verify contact and downstream bus state instead of command echo or elapsed time
reshape regenerative torque before hardware overvoltage containment
prove the envelope with staged fault injection and an energy ledger
private_transfer_gate.publication_policy: The integrated scenario remains private. Each premise maps to causal prose, a Korean-annotated equation, an interactive observable, a failure boundary or an evidence gate.

source_decisions.source: ABB Drives, Technical guide No. 8: Electrical braking
source_decisions.boundary: Industrial AC-drive voltages, load examples, economics and equipment selections do not establish a 48 V battery robot, BMS acceptance, contactor diagnostics, holding brake or certified stop.

source_decisions.source: TI SDAA145A, DC-Link Capacitor Pre-Charge Designs in Automotive Systems
source_decisions.boundary: Automotive high-voltage values and timing targets are topology-specific and do not supply downstream discharge or complete weld diagnostics.

source_decisions.source: TI SLVAFB0, Why Pre-Charge Circuits are Necessary in High-Voltage Systems
source_decisions.boundary: The introductory state sequence is not an independent contactor diagnostic or safety architecture.

source_decisions.source: Sensata, How to Design a Precharge Circuit for Hybrid and Electric Vehicle Applications
used_for: open, welded and active-load diagnostic patterns
source_decisions.boundary: Vendor thresholds and targets are examples; target diagnostic coverage must be measured and allocated separately.

source_decisions.source: TI Stages of motor control and SLLA527
used_for: coast, dynamic, regenerative and resistor braking distinctions
source_decisions.boundary: Introductory driver examples do not size a multi-axis robot braking system.

used_for: bus capacitance, sensing and shutdown handoff
source_decisions.boundary: The board reference does not define the user's payload energy, battery charge allowance, chopper, contactor lifecycle or holding/safety stop.

source_extraction.visual_review: Pages 4, 6, 10, 14, 15 and 23 were inspected as images to preserve the guide's stated purpose, power equation, fan example, capacitor/chopper diagram, listed limitations and common-DC topology.
source_extraction.evidence_boundary: The public ABB lab keeps the published 5 mF, 565-to-735 V, 90 kW, approximately 6 ms example separate from an explicitly illustrative 2.2 mF, 50-to-56 V, 5 kW robot calculation.

events.observed: The power-electronics milestone left both regenerated-energy handling and isolation/EMC/STO as one future hardware-safety bucket.
events.inference: The bucket contained two different causal and evidence systems and would become too broad for a readable bottom-up article.
events.decision: Implement energy/braking first and defer isolation/EMC/STO to the next milestone.
events.verification: The concept has ten energy-to-evidence sections and an explicit safety-certification boundary.

events.observed: A robot can decelerate successfully in one battery state while thirty hidden energy, timing, sink and contactor premises remain false.
events.inference: A list of braking modes would not force the reader to diagnose cross-domain failure.
events.decision: Use a private thirty-premise transfer problem and map every premise before prose generation.
events.verification: The content spec includes the full premise set, section map, formula contract and completion gate.

events.observed: ABB Technical Guide No. 8 supplies a durable mechanics-to-topology decision order but its numerical examples are industrial-drive-specific.
events.inference: The method can become a reference spine only if source conditions and robot adaptation never share one evidence field.
events.decision: Build an ABB evidence selector with source condition, observation, transfer and does-not-transfer fields.
events.verification: The published about-6-ms example and the illustrative robot calculation are visibly separate on mobile and desktop.

events.observed: The mechanisms require different visual observables: topology, quadrant, time, allocation, feasibility, arbitration and state transition.
events.inference: One repeated boxes-and-arrows scene would hide the actual decision variable in several sections.
events.decision: Implement ten distinct interactive labs with stable dimensions and compact metric ledgers.
events.verification: Every concept lab changes visible evidence after a slider or mode interaction on the public host.

events.observed: The first QA run found English-only underbraces such as chopper current, precharge trajectory and stop-time first estimate.
events.inference: A formula could contain some Korean and still violate the requirement that each operation explain itself in Korean.
events.decision: Translate every underbrace label and strengthen QA to inspect every LaTeX text annotation individually.
events.verification: Twenty-five concept and eight reference formulas have no English-only text annotation and each has exactly one FormulaNote.

events.observed: The ABB four-column alternative matrix was bounded but too dense on a 390 px viewport.
events.inference: Scaling or smaller typography would preserve geometry while losing scanability.
events.decision: Use stacked option cards on mobile and retain the comparison table from the small breakpoint upward.
events.verification: Mobile labels remain readable with zero document overflow and zero inner Viz scrolling.

events.observed: A post-deployment metric rerun exposed a font-load-dependent 0.83 formula scale at 390 px despite an earlier 0.85 pass.
events.inference: The long sink list and compound torque equation were semantically overloaded, and QA was sampling before font readiness.
events.decision: Normalize sink allocation as a sum over the valid-sink set, split power-to-torque conversion from the final min operation and wait for document.fonts.ready in QA.
events.verification: Final public minimum scale is 0.78 at 360 px, 0.89 at 390 px and 1.0 at 768/1440 px.

events.observed: Local browser evidence cannot prove the reverse proxy serves the last formula and responsive repair.
events.inference: Completion requires final build, service restart, public route checks and the same browser suite against production.
events.decision: Rebuild, restart cm-blog.service and rerun the strengthened twelve-test suite on the public host.
events.verification: All public routes return 200 and all twelve public tests passed in 21.8 seconds.
